- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and recent price is falling; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven support.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion in early days; if sentiment is neutral or negative, apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in continuation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (e.g., 2+ consecutive), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast based on pure price momentum — override with sentiment-weighted average of 0.27–0.53.
